about.epigraph: Small details make the difference between an interface that works and one that people love.
paragraphs: I am a Software Engineering student at FPT University in Ho Chi Minh City and, since June 2026, a Frontend Developer Intern at VNZ Company. I build web interfaces with Next.js, React and TypeScript, with attention to component architecture, consistent design systems and smooth user experiences.

At VNZ I work on the BMT Decor website. With the HKBDU team I build the frontend of university projects such as Pegaxus and Meetly, and I worked on the frontend of SAVICO AI. On my own I keep small projects for practising fundamentals: a React catalog for learning data fetching, URL state and CI, and a Java library written test-first.
I care about the details users notice — spacing, states, theming, localization — and about code that stays readable as the product grows.

projects.intro: Projects I have committed to, ordered by the number of my commits on each repository's default branch.

pegaxus.title: Pegaxus
pegaxus.tagline: Logistics platform for cross-border racehorse transport
pegaxus.summary: Frontend of a system that brings transport booking, route planning, compliance documentation and billing for cross-border racehorse logistics into one web application, built for the SWP391 course.
pegaxus.problem: Moving a racehorse across borders involves many parties and documents: customers book transport, managers plan primary, contingency and return routes, and each trip needs compliance dossiers, quarantine and customs evidence, and invoices.
pegaxus.approach: A feature-based React 19 and TypeScript app (Vite, React Router) with role-based access. Server state runs through TanStack Query, forms through React Hook Form and Zod, maps through MapLibre GL, and documents are previewed with PDF.js. The landing page is a 3D scene built with React Three Fiber.
highlights: Customer portal: horse profiles, bookings and status history
Transport planning with primary, contingency and return routes on interactive maps
Compliance workflow for dossiers, quarantine and customs evidence
Role-based accounts, invoices and payment workflows

bmt-decor.title: BMT Decor
bmt-decor.tagline: Website for an interior design and construction company
bmt-decor.summary: Website for BMT Decor, which offers interior design, turnkey construction and renovation in Ho Chi Minh City. Built during my internship at VNZ Company.
bmt-decor.problem: The site has to present BMT Decor's services, project portfolio, news and careers, and give visitors a quotation request, a contact page and a capability profile — with an admin area behind it.
bmt-decor.approach: Next.js 16 App Router with one feature module per page: about, services, projects, news, careers, contact, quotation, capability profile and admin. The UI uses Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui and Base UI; Motion, Embla carousels and a page-flip effect handle the moving parts.
highlights: Nine feature modules mapped to App Router routes
Admin area alongside the public site
Animated sections, carousels and a page-flip effect
Light and dark themes with next-themes

savico-ai.title: SAVICO AI
savico-ai.tagline: Construction documents generated from a photo of a land plot
savico-ai.summary: Users photograph a land plot, enter their requirements and receive AI-generated drawings, renderings, cost estimates and construction documents. I worked on the frontend and maintain the preview deployment repository.
savico-ai.problem: The product turns a photo and a list of requirements into a construction dossier through three steps — input, estimate, construction documents — surrounded by a home page, knowledge library, guide and personal dashboard: eleven screens in total.
savico-ai.approach: Next.js 16 App Router with locale-prefixed routes (vi, en) and route groups for landing, auth and dashboard; a proxy handles locale routing and route guards. Environment variables are validated with Zod at startup, and dev-only flags swap the separate .NET REST API for in-browser mocks. OKLCH design tokens drive light, dark and system themes.
highlights: Three-step flow across eleven screens
Vietnamese and English with next-intl
Zod-validated environment with mock auth and mock API flags
TanStack Query and Zustand; React Hook Form with Zod

meetly.title: Meetly
meetly.tagline: Real-time group scheduling with a live heatmap
meetly.summary: A group scheduling app inspired by When2meet. Organizers share a poll link, participants paint their availability on a drag-to-select grid, and a live heatmap highlights the best slots.
meetly.problem: An organizer needs everyone's availability and a clear view of where free times overlap — without asking participants to sign up.
meetly.approach: A React, Vite and TypeScript frontend styled with Tailwind CSS. The grid updates over WebSockets through a SignalR client connected to a .NET 8 Web API (controller, service, repository layers) backed by PostgreSQL.
highlights: Drag-to-paint availability grid
Live heatmap over SignalR WebSockets
No sign-up needed for participants
CI quality workflow on the main and dev branches

ritual-catalog.title: RitualCatalog
ritual-catalog.tagline: A catalog of worship rituals, built to learn React fundamentals
ritual-catalog.summary: A web app listing Vietnamese worship rituals (cúng kiếng) with their time of execution, lunar and solar dates, difficulty and content. I built it to understand how data flows through a React app, and to set up CI/CD.
ritual-catalog.problem: Each ritual has a lunar date, a solar date, a time of day, a difficulty level and reference content. Visitors need to search and filter them; administrators need to manage rituals and users.
ritual-catalog.approach: React, Vite and TypeScript with a generic BaseService over Axios and TanStack Query. Search is debounced with a custom useDebounce hook, and page, search and filter values live in the URL through searchParams, so every view can be shared. GitHub Actions lints and builds each push, a second workflow posts to Discord when CI fails, and the app deploys to Vercel.
highlights: Debounced search, pagination and filters synced to the URL
Generic CRUD service layer with TanStack Query
Authentication, route guards, ritual and user management
GitHub Actions CI with Discord failure alerts; Vercel deployment

math-util.title: Math Utility
math-util.tagline: Part of the JDK math library, rebuilt test-first
math-util.summary: A Maven project that re-implements part of the standard JDK math utilities, developed with Test-Driven Development and Data-Driven Testing in JUnit.
math-util.problem: Practise writing logic test-first: describe the behaviour as tests, then implement until they pass.
math-util.approach: Java and Maven with JUnit Jupiter 5.10. Data-driven tests describe each function, and a GitHub Actions workflow runs the suite on every push.
highlights: Test-Driven and Data-Driven Testing with JUnit 5
Maven build
Continuous integration with GitHub Actions
